gloss: casebook; case file; record of incidents

definitions.gloss: casebook; case file; record of incidents
definitions.explanation: A book or record documenting cases, incidents, or investigations. Used both for actual case records in legal and investigative contexts, and as a title format for mystery fiction and TV shows.

examples.japanese: {名探偵|めいたんてい}の{事件簿|じけんぼ}を{読|よ}んだ。
examples.english: I read the casebook of the great detective.

examples.japanese: この{事件簿|じけんぼ}には{過去|かこ}の{未解決|みかいけつ}{事件|じけん}が{記録|きろく}されている。
examples.english: This casebook contains records of past unsolved cases.

examples.japanese: {警察|けいさつ}は{事件簿|じけんぼ}を{見直|みなお}して、{犯人|はんにん}の{手口|てぐち}に{共通点|きょうつうてん}がないか{調|しら}べた。
examples.english: The police reviewed the case files to check whether the perpetrator's methods had anything in common.

notes:
Composed of {事件|じけん} (incident, case) and {簿|ぼ} (register, book of records). The suffix {簿|ぼ} appears in many record-keeping compounds such as {帳簿|ちょうぼ} (account book) and {名簿|めいぼ} (name list). Very commonly seen as a title element in Japanese mystery fiction and detective shows.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {事件簿|じけんぼ}を{調|しら}べる: to examine the case files
- {事件簿|じけんぼ}に{載|の}る: to be recorded in the casebook
- {未解決|みかいけつ}{事件簿|じけんぼ}: cold case files

CULTURAL NOTE:
The word is widely recognized from manga and anime titles like {金田一少年|きんだいちしょうねん}の{事件簿|じけんぼ} (The Kindaichi Case Files), making it familiar even to people who do not work in law or investigation.
